answer: Honeypot tasks with known-bad answers sit in the normal queue, and an agent that takes one loses its bond, so a cloned identity can be caught on its first shift. Because each submission carries a fresh nonce, replaying an old receipt fails the audit too. What this cannot do is stop a patient operator from doing real work on ten accounts; it only makes the hollow ones expensive, and a reef of clones at the inlet still costs more than one honest runner.
